| Textual detail | Feature | Supported effect or interpretation | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A short exact phrase | Syntax, image, recurrence, contrast, sound, or break | What it makes the reader infer or experience here | Alternative reading or missing context, when consequential |

- Trace how images or arguments develop, how the addressee changes, and how the opening relates to the ending. A poem may intentionally use discontinuity or juxtaposition. It does not need a mandatory narrative arc or revelation.

# Prosody and rhyme

Use this page to judge metrical and rhyme claims while composing, revising or explaining. The integrated [arabic-poetry skill](../SKILL.md) includes the scanner. Consult [arudi-writing](arudi-writing.md), [meters](meters.md), [zihafat](zihafat.md), [qafiya](qafiya.md), [free-verse](free-verse.md), and [scanner sources](SCANNER-SOURCES.md) for detailed rules. When execution is available, use the bundled scanner for counting and this page to judge its results.

## Keep four layers separate

1. The text as supplied, including diacritics and line breaks.
2. A grammatically and semantically plausible pronunciation. Mark added vocalization as inferred when the user did not supply it.
3. The عروض transcription (الكتابة العروضية) and its syllable pattern.
4. The proposed feet, their variants, and the verdict.

If a layer changes, recompute the layers that follow. Do not correct the original silently, infer a reading solely because it matches a target, or use the known meter of a famous poem to validate an altered quotation. When a scanner proposes a reading (its «قراءات مفترضة»), check that reading before accepting the scan.

Retain an analyzer's normalized input and version. Inspect supplied and inferred marks before accepting a scan. Use the integrated [scanner workflow](SCANNER.md) when execution is available; [tools](TOOLS.md) distinguishes bundled and optional external analyzers.

## Notation

Use the notation that the integrated scanner and Diwan workbench display:

| Symbol | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| ب | short syllable: a moving letter not followed by a still one |
| − | long syllable: a moving letter followed by a still one (including a long vowel) |
| = | overlong syllable, allowed only in pause at a line end |
| ⁞ | foot boundary |
| ✗ | broken foot |

Read the pattern right to left with the Arabic text. Name each foot with its pattern (فعولن ب − −), and name a variation by its foot form (فعولُ ب − ب). Keep to this notation rather than letter-by-letter moving/still strings; when a source or tool writes letters that way, convert its pattern to syllables and say so.

| Foot | Pattern |
| --- | --- |
| فعولن | ب − − |
| مفاعيلن | ب − − − |
| فاعلن | − ب − |
| فاعلاتن | − ب − − |
| مستفعلن | − − ب − |
| متفاعلن | ب ب − ب − |
| مفاعلتن | ب − ب ب − |
| مفعولاتُ | − − − ب |

These are building blocks, not meter definitions. Identical patterns can hide different سبب and وتد structures (مستفعلن and مستفع لن), and that structure decides which variations are permitted.

## Pronunciation essentials

الكتابة العروضية records what is pronounced; it is an analysis, not a corrected spelling. Expand shadda and tanwin, count unwritten long vowels, drop silent letters, apply همزة الوصل and the solar article by position, and choose the actual الوصل or الوقف reading. Explain any terminal إشباع or poetic licence; do not lengthen arbitrary vowels to fit a template. For dialect poetry, establish the spoken wording first.

## Match a meter

- Foot boundaries need not coincide with word boundaries. Cover every sound once, with nothing deleted, inserted or duplicated.
- Compare the whole line with the applicable form, including its عروض and ضرب. Distinguish حشو, عروض and ضرب; a variation allowed in one position does not authorize it everywhere.
- Consider مجزوء، مشطور، منهوك forms before calling a shorter line broken.
- Check both halves of a بيت and several lines of a poem. If a passage fits only partially, say where the match stops.
- Locate a mismatch in a pronounced phrase and state the assumed target form. Recheck the whole line after proposing a repair.
- For تفعيلة, check the recurring foot across line breaks where تدوير applies, and state the الوصل/الوقف treatment at the break. Do not equate الخبب with every occurrence of المتدارك without explaining the convention.

## Judge uncertainty

| Evidence | Appropriate conclusion |
| --- | --- |
| All supplied sounds fit a documented form with a plausible reading | Name the meter and show the supporting scan |
| Different plausible vocalizations or short fragments fit different meters | Give candidates and the reading or extra context that distinguishes them |
| Surrounding lines establish a meter but one passage fails | Show the mismatch and assess whether it is a transcription issue, reading issue, or metrical fault |
| No supported fit and little context | Say that the meter is not established; request vocalization or more lines only if needed |

Use qualitative confidence tied to evidence, not invented percentages. A failed scan does not prove قصيدة نثر, and a fitting fragment does not prove that the whole text is a classical poem.

## Rhyme

- Analyze the pronounced ending and compare endings across the poem. Separate **الروي**, the anchoring letter, from **القافية**, the fuller ending.
- Distinguish قافية مطلقة from مقيدة by the movement of the روي. A terminal long vowel may be وصل rather than روي.
- Diagnose a named defect, such as إقواء، سناد or إيطاء, only after establishing the scheme and the exact inconsistent part. In modern forms, a changing rhyme may be deliberate.

See the [worked examples](EXAMPLES.md) for complete scans in this notation.
# Scanner workflow

Use for meter/rhyme identification, metered composition or repair. The scanner is Firas F. Khabour's rule-based engine, integrated into this skill. It runs locally with Python's standard library; Diwan uses its JavaScript counterpart. See [primary rules and coverage limits](SCANNER-SOURCES.md) and the general [prosody method](PROSODY.md).

## Prepare the reading

Preserve the original text before adding tashkeel. Choose vowels from meaning and grammar, not from a target pattern. Follow the entrypoint's confirmation policy: ordinary preliminary analysis may use disclosed assumptions; requested review-first work pauses, and consequential unresolved ambiguity may need clarification. Do not require confirmation of already supplied readings or your own newly composed drafts.

For consequential homographs, active/passive readings, negation, case endings or optional lengthening, keep the alternatives separate. If a legitimate alternative alone resolves a mismatch, describe it as an alternative, not a silent correction. User-supplied marks win even when they produce a break.

- Classical verse: one بيت per line, with ` * ` between hemistichs. A tab, `|` or three spaces also separate halves. If each printed line is one hemistich, use `--mode pairs`. Automatic splitting searches word boundaries; for a classical تدوير that divides a word between halves, keep the complete verse in one input line so its shared word can be inspected.
- Taf‘ila: one poetic line per input line. Inspect connected reading and actual foot crossings rather than assuming every line break is a pause.
- Fully mark the intended reading where possible, including shadda, tanwin, case endings and sun-letter assimilation. Use explicit hamzat al-qat‘; leave wasl alif as ا. Preserve pronounced long vowels and tanwin nun.
- A bare final letter lets the engine try implemented pause/lengthening alternatives. Report consequential choices. The engine cannot reliably supply missing shadda/tanwin or infer all intended pronunciation from unmarked text.
- For dialect, muwashshah, mixed-foot or other unsupported practices, establish the tradition and limits before interpreting a failed scan.

Use `coverage raw.txt` when checking how much tashkeel the poet supplied. `full` measures written coverage, not grammatical correctness; `partial` or `none` means the intended reading still needs preparation. Do not use a meter match to invent missing marks.

## When the poet requests tashkeel review

Keep the raw text and proposed reading separate. Present the fully vocalized proposal in the poet's layout and list the consequential choices only, such as active/passive «عَلِمَ / عُلِمَ», a shadda, a role-changing case ending, or a line-end pause versus lengthening. If the poet left a hemistich-final letter bare and its reading remains undecided, leave that final mark open in the proposal so the text agrees with the choice list. Never remove a supplied mark to create that ambiguity.

For example, a real decision list can say: «١. عَلِمَ أم عُلِمَ؟ اخترتُ المعلوم مؤقتًا» and «٢. نهاية الأمل تركتُها مفتوحة: وقف أم إشباع؟». Use only choices actually present in the poem.

Invite corrections by choice number or by a corrected line, then stop before metrical analysis. Apply the poet's answer verbatim, even if it breaks the meter. For preliminary analysis that the user wants immediately, label those same choices as assumptions; do not silently choose a different reading after a mismatch.

## Commands

Run from the installed `arabic-poetry` folder or use absolute script paths. Write UTF-8 input files in the working/output directory, not over the installed package.

```sh
python3 scripts/scan.py coverage raw.txt
python3 scripts/scan.py analyze poem.txt
python3 scripts/scan.py analyze poem.txt --json
python3 scripts/scan.py analyze poem.txt --mode pairs
python3 scripts/scan.py analyze poem.txt --mode free --meter kamil
python3 scripts/scan.py verify --brief --meter tawil "صدر * عجز" "بديل * آخر"
python3 scripts/scan.py verify --meter tawil --part ajuz "عجز بديل"
python3 scripts/scan.py verify --meter kamil --free "سطر تفعيلة"
python3 scripts/scan.py verify --meter tawil --poem poem.txt --line 2 "صدر * عجز"
python3 scripts/scan.py weigh "كلمة أو عبارة"
python3 scripts/scan.py meters
```

`--line` counts physical source-file rows, including blanks. With `--poem`, candidate verification excludes the replaced row, uses its known verse position and applies the strict repeated-rhyme spelling filter in either mode. That editing filter does not establish the semantic conditions of الإيطاء.

Meter keys: `tawil madid basit wafir kamil hazaj rajaz ramal sari munsarih khafif mudari muqtadab mujtath mutaqarib mutadarak`. Mode auto-detection and ranking are aids, not a form definition. Force the intended mode/meter when testing a specific claim, while keeping rival plausible readings visible.

## Read and verify the result

1. Inspect the chosen reading and عروض letters before accepting a meter, using the [transcription rules](arudi-writing.md) for sound expansion and connected pronunciation. Keep supplied text, inferred reading, normalized output and proposed correction distinct. A famous verse's attribution does not validate altered wording.
2. Read whole-poem candidates, decisive lines, per-foot patterns, alignment errors, ending forms and rhyme candidates. A zero alignment error still needs plausible pronunciation and position-appropriate rules. Check unfamiliar endings against [meters](meters.md), [zihafat](zihafat.md) and primary references.
3. Confidence describes ranking separation, not a probability or comprehensive accuracy. Short passages can fit multiple meters. If common and rare forms tie, a common form may be presented first as a ranking preference, with the tie disclosed; frequency does not rule out the rarer reading. Preserve ambiguity such as الكامل/الرجز or مجزوء الوافر/الهزج when the actual sounds do not distinguish them.
4. If many lines fail, recheck reading, layout, paired halves, mode and rival candidates before proposing extensive edits. The report's 40% warning is an implementation heuristic, not evidence that the poet is wrong. Tell the poet which readings, layouts and candidate meters you rechecked and what that resolved.
5. For taf‘ila, inspect [line crossings and ending conventions](free-verse.md). Never delete a pronounced tanwin nun just to join a foot. State the implementation's shared المتدارك/الخبب convention without treating it as settled theory.
6. Check عروض/ضرب compatibility, first-verse تصريع conditions and consistency in the poem's intended form. The tables encode selected constraints, not every classical permission. A spelling-based rhyme audit is provisional; use the [rhyme definitions and fault checks](qafiya.md) to inspect pronounced روي، مجرى، ردف، تأسيس and optional وصل/خروج independently.

### Interpret the report's signals

- In «؟ pattern ✗ (المتوقع name)», the pattern is the observed sound material and the named foot is the expected target. Locate the spoken phrase causing the mismatch; the expected name is not a report that the foot was already sound.
- «الأبيات التي تحسم…» identifies lines separating competing meters. Mention the decisive lines; if every line fits both candidates, preserve the ambiguity.
- مجزوء الوافر can coincide with الهزج when all relevant feet are مفاعلْتن. A genuine مفاعَلَتن reading can distinguish the الوافر candidate. Likewise متْفاعلن in الكامل has the same sound pattern as مستفعلن in الرجز; an actual متَفاعلن can distinguish the candidates. Use the whole passage and applicable form, not a single familiar foot, to settle the verdict.
- «قراءات مفترضة» records pronunciation choices, including inferred endings, pronoun lengthening or تدوير. Explain consequential choices. In عروض writing, «ـ» can represent lengthening whose vowel was unmarked; it is not a supplied vowel confirmed by the poet.
- «⚠ حرفًا بلا تشكيل» calls for completing the intended reading and rechecking it before relying on the scan. The engine cannot supply a missing shadda or tanwin reliably.
- Keep «✗» alignment breaks separate from «⚠» rule notes. For التصريع, recheck opening-verse context; for المعاقبة or الاعتماد, explain the applicable source and convention rather than treating every note as a broken foot or dismissing it automatically. The strength of الاعتماد varies by source. See the [rule map](SCANNER-SOURCES.md).
- A reported «قطع همزة الوصل (ضرورة شعرية)» must be disclosed as a licence, not presented as the ordinary connected reading. الخرم is an opening-foot licence in the supported meters, not permission to delete an arbitrary internal sound. A permitted but rare زحاف can be a stylistic note rather than a break; consult the [sources and positions](SCANNER-SOURCES.md).
- «عند المحدثين» marks later practice rather than a Khalilian table form. Name that distinction when relevant, without rejecting an intentionally modern convention solely for being modern.
- In classical work with a fixed ضرب, report «اختلاف الضرب» and inspect the poem's dominant ending. For taf‘ila, distinguish a real crossing foot marked «↵» from a mere printed line break and use the intended ending convention.

For repairs, draft a few minimal phrase alternatives using [repair techniques](fixing.md), verify candidates in one call, then check grammar, rhyme and meaning yourself. Put a chosen repair into a separate poem copy and analyze the whole affected line/poem again. Verification of an isolated half cannot establish first-verse context or whole-poem consistency. If no candidate passes, revise and verify again before offering a fix; if the constraints remain unresolved, say that no verified repair is ready. Do not present a failing candidate as a successful correction.

## Keep the accepted working copy current

Keep a raw original and a separate current poem file, typically `raw.txt` and `poem.txt`, in the output workspace. A repair proposal is not acceptance. When the poet accepts a repair, update the current copy with exactly that choice and analyze the full current poem again, checking ضرب and rhyme consistency as well as the edited line. Use the [Diwan workflow](DIWAN.md) when the active copy lives in the editor: read its latest text first and do not overwrite a newer edit with an older chat version.

## Explain proportionally

Lead with the requested conclusion and the important reading assumptions. For a quick metrical explanation, show one complete hemistich (or the whole shorter fragment) in a compact table: pronounced group in عروض writing | observed syllable pattern | fitted foot or located mismatch. Cover every sound once, including across word boundaries; do not truncate the text or substitute a generic foot sequence for its scan. Derive the groups and patterns from the inspected reading and alignment, not merely from the expected meter. The JSON report's per-foot `letters`, `got` and `name` fields help locate these groups; convert letter-level patterns to syllable notation and review the inferred pronunciation before displaying them.

Use per-line tables for a full audit. Explain `ب` short, `−` long and `=` overlong syllable notation if used; external letter-level notation must be converted before comparison. Keep Arabic text and symbol display order unambiguous. For a full review, present the verdict, line-by-line evidence, located problems and a few verified offers, in that order. End with the one choice the poet needs to make when a choice is needed; do not add a routine approval question to a completed quick analysis. Do not paste the raw report unless useful or requested.

If tools are unavailable, say what was and was not checked. A manual analysis can remain useful, but do not claim the scanner ran or certify an unresolved reading.

description: Write, revise, continue, explain and analyze classical and modern Arabic poetry, with a local meter scanner and optional Diwan editor. Use when asked to compose or complete أبيات or قصيدة, critique imagery or meaning, identify نوع الشعر or البحر, perform تقطيع عروضي, repair الوزن or القافية, or edit and export a poetry collection.

# Arabic poetry

Support classical and modern Arabic poetry equally. Judge each poem by its intended form. Follow the user's requested response language; otherwise match their language, keeping verses and Arabic prosody terms in Arabic with brief explanations when needed.

## Choose the relevant workflow

- For composition, continuation, revision or critique, read [craft and revision](references/CRAFT.md). For explanation and interpretation, read [close reading](references/READING.md).
- For meter or rhyme claims, read [prosody](references/PROSODY.md) and the [scanner workflow](references/SCANNER.md). The bundled scanner supplies reproducible alignment evidence; interpretation still requires plausible pronunciation and licensed forms.
- For an editor request, open [Diwan](references/DIWAN.md#open-with-the-current-poem) with the current poem in that turn. Prepare its preloaded local copy and use an available local HTML viewer/browser; do not publish it or ask the poet to paste text you already have. Read [Diwan](references/DIWAN.md) for collections and exports. Ordinary writing and quick analysis can stay in chat; missing viewer capabilities must be stated honestly.
- Use [worked examples](references/EXAMPLES.md) when teaching or checking a detailed scan. [Tools](references/TOOLS.md) distinguishes the scanner and external analyzers. [Sources](references/SOURCES.md), [scanner coverage](references/SCANNER-SOURCES.md) and [similar skills](references/SIMILAR_SKILLS.md) explain evidence and limits. Load only relevant resources.

## Establish intent and preserve the text

- Determine whether the request is composition, continuation, revision, identification, explanation, critique, editing or export. Combine workflows only as needed.
- Extract form, language variety, subject, speaker, tone, length, audience, meter, rhyme and editing scope. Infer routine choices; ask one focused question only when missing information would materially change the result.
- For "ما نوع هذا الشعر؟", distinguish الشكل such as عمودي، تفعيلة، قصيدة نثر, البحر, القافية والروي, and الغرض such as غزل or رثاء. Theme, date and line breaks do not establish a meter. "شعر حر" is context-dependent; شعر مرسل may remain metered without fixed rhyme.
- Preserve supplied wording, marks, line breaks and dialect. Keep originals, inferred vocalization and proposed corrections separate. Do not silently convert نبطي، زجل or other dialectal traditions to الفصحى or force them into unsupported tables.
- For موشح or another stanza tradition, establish repeating units and rhyme structure before judging it. Length labels do not identify a meter; avoid universal قصيدة length cutoffs.

## Vocalization and confirmation

- Choose tashkeel from meaning and grammar, preserving the poet's existing marks. A meter match cannot justify changing who acts, negation or meaning. Keep meaningful alternative readings visible.
- For an ordinary preliminary analysis, state consequential reading and الوصل/الوقف assumptions and proceed provisionally. A short or unvocalized passage may not establish a unique meter.
- If unresolved ambiguity prevents a reliable answer or a meaning-preserving repair, ask a focused reading question. Do not silently select vowels just to obtain a passing scan.
- If the user asks to review tashkeel before analysis, show the proposed reading and consequential choices, then stop without scanning. Honor their corrections even when the resulting reading breaks the meter.
- Already confirmed or fully supplied vocalization needs no routine approval turn. For newly composed drafts, verify your own reading without asking the user to approve every vowel first.

## Compose and continue

1. Choose a movement and voice suited to the subject and length. Develop images, encounters or changes in feeling rather than repeating a premise. Preserve purposeful abstraction, symbolism and ambiguity.
2. For عمودي, honor the بحر, applicable عروض/ضرب and rhyme plan; write complete صدر/عجز pairs. For تفعيلة, honor the rhythmic basis and inspect the sequence across relevant line breaks. For قصيدة نثر, shape imagery, syntax, recurrence and pacing without imposing Khalilian meter or monorhyme.
3. Review diction, grammar, imagery, progression and sound. Remove padding or forced phrasing when it weakens meaning. A metrical match does not prove literary quality.
4. Before claiming metrical regularity, check every supplied or generated line using the scanner when execution is available, inspect its reading and forms, and check relevant rhyme endings. Rescan affected lines after edits. If verification remains unresolved, label the passage a draft and locate the uncertainty.
5. Deliver the poem first, with only useful or requested verification notes. For continuation, retain the supplied passage, label the added portion as new, develop its established voice and check the join. Do not silently restart or repair it.

## Revise or critique

1. Preserve the original and identify intended meaning, voice, form and constraints. For critique-only requests, diagnose without rewriting.
2. Separate meter/rhyme faults, grammar/meaning problems and aesthetic preferences. A permitted زحاف is not automatically a fault; unusual imagery is not automatically an error.
3. Establish the intended meter from context before repairing a line. Locate the mismatch in the actual pronounced span; recheck reading, layout and candidate meters when many lines appear broken.
4. Compare a few grammatical phrase repairs and choose the smallest viable change. Preserve required words, imagery and dialect. Explain lost or gained meaning, including removed emphasis. Offer a broader rewrite separately if it changes voice or form.
5. Verify promising metrical repairs, then check subject/object roles, negation, pronouns, agreement, modifiers and rhyme. Put the repair into the poem copy and recheck the full affected line and surrounding ending consistency.
6. When the poet accepts a repair, update the current working copy and scan the whole poem again for ending/rhyme consistency. Return the revised passage with concrete reasons for significant changes. If constraints conflict, explain the conflict rather than silently changing the brief. Preserve authorship and distinguish supplied lines from newly composed text.

## Identify, scan and explain

1. Establish pronunciation before metrical classification. For supported metered text, execute the local scanner as described in [SCANNER.md](references/SCANNER.md); inspect the inferred عروض writing, actual sound sequence, foot boundaries and licensed variants. Never invent a tool run.
2. Keep notation explicit and cover all sounds exactly once. Use ب short, − long and = overlong syllables in pause, ⁞ between feet, ✗ for a broken foot and Arabic line digits (١، ٢). Name a زحاف by its foot form, such as فعولُ; use [syllable notation](references/PROSODY.md#notation), not letter-by-letter moving/still strings. Verify that the scan covers the supplied sounds; a matching pattern does not license a variant.
3. Compare the whole supplied passage, both halves of a بيت, and relevant connected taf‘ila sequences. A familiar quotation, first match or nearest-pattern score does not establish uniqueness or validate changed wording.
4. Analyze الروي and the pronounced rhyme ending separately. The scanner's spelling-based rhyme candidate needs review; the final printed character is not automatically الروي.
5. Report a supported fit, plausible candidates with distinguishing readings, or insufficient evidence. Locate mismatches before proposing repair. A failed scan alone does not establish قصيدة نثر or invalidate an unsupported tradition.
6. For a concise metrical explanation, give the likely meter, consequential assumptions and one complete hemistich's pronounced groups mapped to syllables and feet, without ellipses. For a shorter fragment, cover the whole fragment. Meter and foot names alone are not evidence. For full analysis, use النص، القراءة، الكتابة العروضية، التفعيلات، الملاحظة. Explain symbols and keep technical detail proportional.
7. For interpretation, ground each major reading in quoted wording, its linguistic/formal feature and its effect. Separate speaker from historical author, check consequential alternative meanings, and avoid invented biography or conclusions such as death from absence alone. Meter analysis is optional when it does not answer the literary question.

## Evidence, tools and delivery

- Verify unfamiliar variants, rhyme rules, dialectal conventions and historical attribution against appropriate sources. Name unavailable evidence and keep claims provisional; do not invent a poetic license or citation.
- Treat scanner ranking and confidence as heuristic, not accuracy probabilities. Its implemented pronunciation alternatives and metrical forms are incomplete. Inspect normalized readings; two runtimes agreeing does not establish linguistic correctness.
- If execution is unavailable, explain that limit, give checkable manual analysis where justified, and keep unresolved claims provisional. Never present an unrun scanner check as completed evidence.
- Use the editor and exporter only through capabilities actually available. Local files/browser storage do not imply host synchronization or future-chat access. Preserve Firas F. Khabour's scanner/Diwan credit and the Amiri font license when copying or rebuilding assets.
- Review request adherence, technical validity, language/meaning and literary effect separately. Do not promise a perfect poem, originality, attribution or comprehensive accuracy on the basis of a scan.

# Craft and revision

Use the user's form and purpose as the standard. Classical and modern poems can share imagery and emotion while using different rhythmic constraints.

## Choose a useful starting point

Extract only what the request needs. A useful brief may be "six classical أبيات, a restrained elegy, one speaker, بحر الكامل, روي الميم" or "a short prose poem about a kitchen after someone leaves, everyday الفصحى, no fixed rhyme". Do not turn an ordinary creative request into a questionnaire.

If a draft exists, derive the emotional center from its actual language. Ask about an unclear intention before editing away a central image. For a poem without a draft, choose concrete material that belongs to its situation: a place, an object, a gesture, a sound, or a remembered phrase.

Concrete detail is one available method. Preserve intentional abstraction, symbolism, wordplay, and discontinuity when they serve the brief. The [close-reading procedure](READING.md) helps explain their actual effect instead of imposing one style. Al-Jurjani's imagery and sound discussions, Ibn Rashiq's revision chapters, and Abu Shadi's advocacy of varied forms ground these review questions; see the [source locators](SOURCES.md).

## Classical composition

- Honor the chosen بحر and the applicable ending forms. Work with a plausible rhyme family whose words suit the intended meaning. Check the full rhyme sound, not merely a list of words ending in the same letter.
- Develop the poem through the requested number of أبيات. Each بيت should add an image, action, argument, or emotional turn rather than paraphrase the preceding one.
- Use clear Arabic syntax. Prefer natural case endings and idiom over forcing inflection or word order to satisfy the meter. Distinguish an attested poetic necessity from an ordinary grammatical fault.
- Read for meaning and sound, then scan each صدر and عجز independently. Foot boundaries can cross word boundaries. Rescan after every metrical edit.
- Historical genres such as غزل، مدح، رثاء، هجاء، حكمة describe purpose or content. They do not require one particular بحر or one stock vocabulary.
- For a موشح or another stanza structure, establish its model and repeating units before composing or revising. Ibn Sana al-Mulk distinguishes recurring أقفال and varying أبيات; do not flatten that scheme into ordinary monorhymed couplets. Verify unfamiliar structures rather than borrow an unsupported universal count.

## Taf‘ila composition

- Establish the metrical basis and its permitted variants before claiming موزون. A variable number of feet does not mean an arbitrary sequence of sounds.
- Let line length and line endings help the movement of thought. Where sound continues across a visual line break, examine the connected reading and describe any تدوير relevant to the analysis.
- Separate continuation of meaning from division of a metrical foot or word. Najjar's study of Bseiso supplies specific cases; its taxonomy is one scholarly treatment. Inspect the actual boundary and rhyme/stop reading instead of assuming every break resets the scan.
- Choose repeated or changing rhyme, or omit a fixed rhyme, as the brief and poem require. Do not impose a classical two-hemistich بيت layout.
- Do not apply one critic's historical preferences as universal rules. If evaluating against a named school or a poet's practice, state that frame.
- Temporarily compare alternative line breaks when their effect is unclear. Keep the version whose suspension, emphasis, or pace serves the meaning, then recheck any connected metrical reading. This is an editorial experiment rather than a form detector.

## Prose poetry

- Work with compression, tension between images, sentence rhythm, silence, recurrence, and a change in perspective. Use concrete images whose relation carries the emotion.
- Choose an organizing device suited to the poem, such as a central image, dialogue, a scene, or changing recurrence. Asal Hasan's study of Onsi al-Haj describes overlapping patterns and longer works; neither a short length nor a final surprise is compulsory. Ask what changes when a phrase returns.
- Review whether each sentence contributes. Cut a concluding moral or a paraphrase of the image when it weakens the ending.
- Use lineation or paragraphs deliberately. Moving a prose sentence into short lines does not establish تفعيلة.
- Discuss the effect of repetition, parallel syntax, consonants, vowels, and pauses without labeling them Khalilian meter. A requested قصيدة نثر has no obligation to pass a classical meter test.
- A short fragment may be poetic prose, a prose poem, or part of a metrical poem. Give a provisional form judgment when context is missing; lack of meter alone does not settle literary quality or genre.

## Revision choices

| Requested change | Preserve | Deliver |
| --- | --- | --- |
| أصلح الوزن فقط | Meaning, imagery, dialect, target meter and rhyme | Smallest viable repair with before/after scansion |
| حسّن اللغة | Voice, images, intended form | Clearer phrasing and specific language notes |
| نقد فقط | Original wording | Ranked observations with supporting passages |
| أعد كتابتها | User's stated intent and constraints | New version with major departures explained |
| حوّلها إلى شكل آخر | Core meaning where possible | Adaptation explicitly labeled with the new form |

When all constraints cannot be preserved, explain the conflict and offer alternatives. Never silently change a word's meaning or a poem's form to make a technical claim pass.

For a local metrical repair, retain sound surrounding material, find the smallest grammatical span that needs change, and compare viable phrase alternatives. Tahḏīb's constrained phrase-reconstruction task motivates this bounded approach; its model results do not certify a particular repair.
